qt: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

On 11 May 2026, units of the Libyan coastguard opened fire on the civilian rescue vessel ‘Sea-Watch 5’ – which had just performed a rescue operation in international waters – and threatened to tow it to Libya. The incident occurred despite earlier assurances from the Commission that it had stepped up monitoring and dialogue mechanisms in the wake of the attack on the rescue vessel ‘Ocean Viking’ in August 2025. Reports of severe violence against migrants in Libya at the hands of civilian, state and quasi-state actors are currently on the rise. 1.

Under which framework (EU-funded programmes, cooperation frameworks or EUbacked bilateral agreements) did the EU supply, retrofit, maintain, co-finance or otherwise support the vessels involved in the incident (patrol boats 101, 662 ‘Murzuq’ and 648 ‘Ras Jadir’)?

What specific steps has the Commission taken since the attack on the ‘Ocean Viking’ in August 2025 to bolster its monitoring and dialogue mechanisms with the Libyan authorities, what incidents have been dealt with and what consequences ensued?

What criteria does the Commission use to decide whether incidents warrant the suspension, cutting or discontinuation of EU funding, training, equipment support or operational cooperation, and does it consider the aforementioned incident to be an escalation that necessitates changes to the current approach?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.10.2026) The EU-funded programme SIBMMIL1, co-financed with Italy, supported the strengthening of Libyan capacity to conduct search and rescue operations at sea, in line with applicable international human rights obligations, standards, and international maritime law. Support included the provision, refurbishment and maintenance of search and rescue vessels, capacitybuilding activities and trainings. In this context, two refurbished Corrubia-class vessels were supplied. The EU has not received investigative evidence confirming the involvement of one of the two vessels in the mentioned incident. Following the incident involving the Ocean Viking in August 2025, the EU Delegation raised the matter with the Libyan authorities and urged them to verify the facts and responsibilities and to take all necessary measures to ensure compliance with national and international obligations. The authorities informed the EU that they were investigating. The EU has continued to raise the need for compliance with international standards in regular meetings with the Libyan authorities and implementing partners. In case of any incident, such as the one raised, this is also addressed in the framework of the regular technical dialogue on migration, ongoing since 2024. Respect for human rights and international law is a fundamental element of EU external action and of cooperation with Libya. Information from monitoring and dialogue is taken into account when assessing and adapting EU assistance. Where incidents are reported, the Commission raises its concerns with the competent authorities and calls for appropriate follow-up.
1 ‘Support to Integrated Border and Migration Management in Libya’, T05-EUTF-NOA-LY/T05.213 and T05-
